title: Acceptance tests assert on exact output-string fragments (implementation-coupled)
evidence: test_soccer.py:96 asserts output.splitlines()[1].startswith("1. Neymar Jr - Overall: 92"); test_soccer.py:81 asserts "Matches: 19"; test_soccer.py:110 pins ("Flamengo",90,28). These bind to format_player()/team_record() string layout, so any wording change breaks the test without a behaviour change.
suggestion: Assert on parsed/structured values via a thin DSL layer rather than literal rendered substrings.

title: Tests reach below the SUT into internal data-layer structures
evidence: test_soccer.py:90 inspects db.head_to_head(...) dict keys (a_wins/b_wins/draws); test_soccer.py:46-52 asserts db.by_source[...] internals and len(db.players)==18207. These couple tests to SoccerDB internals, not the MCP-tool contract.
suggestion: Exercise behaviour through the MCP tool surface (as test_mcp_stdio does) and keep internal-structure checks to a minimal unit layer.

title: Only 1 of 26 scenario tests uses the real MCP transport; the rest call Python functions directly
evidence: test_soccer.py:65-195 call server.search_matches(...)/db.*(...) in-process; only test_soccer.py:199 test_mcp_stdio drives JSON-RPC over stdio. The 'acceptance' band therefore bypasses the protocol driver it claims to test.
suggestion: Route the q01-q25 scenarios through a shared protocol driver built on the test_mcp_stdio seam so they verify the deployed interface.

title: Scenarios depend on a large pile of pre-loaded real-world data with magic-number assertions
evidence: test_soccer.py:52 len(db.players)==18207 (exact); test_soccer.py:110 Flamengo 2019 = 90 pts/28 wins; test_soccer.py:182 2003 champion == Cruzeiro. Any dataset refresh silently breaks these without indicating a code defect.
suggestion: Derive expected values from the loaded data or use small curated fixtures for deterministic scenarios.

title: Ships 20 MCP tools, well beyond the 12 pinned requirements
evidence: server.py:274 TOOLS registers derbies, bracket, relegated, cup_finals, compare_seasons, best_records, top_scoring_teams, brazilian_clubs_players, team_profile (cross-dataset) in addition to the required match/team/player/standings/stats/h2h tools.
suggestion: No action — noted as scope beyond spec; broad surface widens the test-maintenance burden flagged above.

title: Zero third-party dependencies (stdlib csv + hand-rolled JSON-RPC, no MCP SDK)
evidence: server.py:1-12 implements the MCP lifecycle directly; soccer_data.py:7 uses only csv. No requirements.txt/pyproject.toml present.
suggestion: No action — simplifies the build (test_coverage=0.86, defect_rate=0.959 from scores.json).
